answer: Tundra Beacon Ledger. Each agent must periodically transmit a reading from a co-located hardware sensor whose calibration is bound to a physically unclonable jade microchip; the reading includes ambient conditions that vary unpredictably by location. A raven-shaped checksum ties each transmission to prior chip state, so copied readings fail. An attacker must acquire and field one distinct physical chip per identity, paying hardware, shipping, and maintenance costs that scale linearly with sybil count.
